page: Microsoft Azure F16ams_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Famsv7 family. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 48 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is premium storage capable and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the F16ams_v7 exhibits top-tier single-core performance, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng single-core CPU tests and Geekbench single-core scores. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, also rank in the top 10%. Multi-core performance is average, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores falling in the middle 50%. Memory performance is strong, with the PassMark memory score in the top 25% and uncached read memory bandwidth reaching 103.83 GB/sec. For lightweight machine learning workloads, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 446.22 tokens/sec using a small 135M LLM model, though performance scales down to average for larger 7B and 70B models.

Given its high memory density of 8.0 GB per core and dedicated AMD EPYC processor, the F16ams_v7 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local storage or GPU acceleration. The absence of bundled local storage means storage costs are decoupled, allowing users to scale premium remote storage independently. This server is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, single-threaded processing pipelines, text and image processing, and lightweight language model inference.
